title: Perihelion staging and video-readiness checkpoint
content:
Tonight's Perihelion pass was a practical staging checkpoint with one clear forward-looking question attached: if FFmpeg is now available on both computers, what would it actually take to adapt video into the archive instead of just treating it like an unknown file type?

What changed:

  • Staging defaults opened up: the Resize Dimensions and Compress File Size controls now start expanded by default, so the most common export options are visible immediately instead of requiring two extra clicks on every visit.
  • Left-rail summary added: staging now ends with a compact summary card showing whether the source is the server library or a local folder, how many items are selected, how many are missing, and the image/video/other-file breakdown. When file sizes are available, the same card also reports the total known size of the current selection.
  • Video support was mapped honestly: Peri already recognizes video extensions and can serve those files through the protected backend routes, but thumbnail generation is still image-only and the frontend still treats video as a managed file rather than as previewable media.

Why this matters: the staging screen is now easier to use during real export sessions, and the media review gives us a clean next step for video instead of folding it into the app blindly. The sensible path from here is browser playback first, FFmpeg poster thumbnails second, and optional video-specific compression/transcode tooling later.
